extracted.intended_audience: general U.S. public / eligible registrants and local officials
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report and reproduction of President Roosevelt's proclamation and explanatory text describing the procedures, duties, exemptions, classification, and selection rules under the Selective Training and Service Act (first registration Oct 16, 1940).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration date and hours
rubrics_metrics.description: "The first registration under the selective training and service act of 1940 shall take place on Wednesday, the sixteenth day of October, 1940, between the hours of 7 a. m. and 9 p. m."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies exact date and hours for the first registration; times and places for Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico will be fixed in subsequent proclamations; special regulations will be prescribed for those unable to register on the date because of sickness or other causes beyond their control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons required to register (age and status)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every male person ... who, on the day or days fixed for the first or any subsequent registration, is between the ages of twenty-one and thirty-five, to present himself for and submit to registration"; applies to male citizens and male aliens residing in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those within the continental U.S. must register on the designated date at the designated place in their registration area; those not within the continental U.S. on that date must register within five days after return; every person subject to registration is required to familiarize himself with and comply with the rules and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from registration / relieved categories
rubrics_metrics.description: (Sec. 5(A) list) Commissioned officers, warrant officers, pay clerks, and enlisted men of the regular Army, the Navy, the Marine Corps, the Coast Guard, the Coast and Geodetic Survey, the Public Health Service, the Federally recognized active National Guard, Officers' Reserve Corps, regular Army Reserve, Enlisted Reserve Corps, Naval Reserve and Marine Corps Reserve; cadets, midshipmen, Coast Guard Academy cadets (during the continuance of acceptance); members of ROTC/NROTC advanced courses; and certain foreign diplomatic/consular representatives who are not U.S. citizens and have not declared intent to become citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text frames these as exceptions "except as otherwise provided in this act" and indicates such persons "shall not be required to be registered under Section 2.. and shall be relieved from liability for training and service under Section 5(A)"; consult act sections for full scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration place / residence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must present themselves for registration "at the duly designated place of registration within the precinct, district, or registration area in which he has his permanent home or in which he may happen to be on that date."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If outside continental U.S. on the date, registrant must register within five days after return; regulations will provide for special registration of those unable to appear on the fixed date due to sickness or other causes beyond control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration procedure: card and certificate handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Each registrant will fill out a registration card and a registration certificate; "The registration card... will be forwarded to the county clerk or a similar official and delivered by him to the local selective service board." The certificate is carried by the registrant as testimonial to acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration cards will be kept by local boards; cards may be shuffled and assigned numbers; order of selection will be entered on the registration cards in custody of local boards and used in subsequent selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Selective Service Boards: composition and appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: Local selective service boards will consist of three men each, appointed by the President upon the recommendation of State Governors, and will be set up in more than 6,000 communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proclamation calls upon Governors and Board of Commissioners of D.C. to provide suitable and sufficient places and registration boards; boards are charged with receiving cards, determining classification and selection, and administering local quotas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory boards for registrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory boards for registrants, "composed of patriotic citizens, civilian volunteers, will be organized in every community in the land."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to assist registrants in presenting fairly the facts to be used in determining the place of every individual in the scheme of national defense; advisory boards will help registrants complete questionnaires and present supporting facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification into four classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Local boards, after due consideration of questionnaires, will place registrants in one of four classes: "In class one... available for immediate service; in class two... deferred because of the essential character of the service they are rendering in their present occupations; in class three... those individuals who should be deferred because of individuals dependent upon them for support; in class four, those specifically deferred by the terms of the act."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those in deferred classes (II, III, IV) will not be called unless there are not enough Class I men to meet the Army's needs; classification depends on facts provided in questionnaires and investigations by local boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority selection by drawing and quotas
rubrics_metrics.description: A national drawing by lot will determine the order of priority of the registrants in each local board area; "The total number of individuals needed by the armed forces will be prorated among the several states... within each state a quota... will be divided among the local boards."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local boards shuffle registration cards, draw series of numbers, and the first numbers drawn determine the order of liability for service; priority lists and order of selection are entered on registration cards and control mailing of questionnaires and subsequent calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionnaires and information for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Questionnaires will be mailed to registrants asking number of dependents, physical disabilities, and other pertinent facts; "Upon receipt of these questionnaires the registrant will enter on them pertinent facts to be used in making final classifications of the registrants according to their qualifications for service."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant must supply accurate information; advisory boards assist registrants in presenting facts; local boards use questionnaire data to assign class; registrants must familiarize themselves with rules and comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteering for one-year service and priority acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: In each local board area "individuals between the ages of eighteen and thirty-five will be offered the opportunity to volunteer for a one-year period of service and training. Such applicants will be accepted before any other individuals are selected, provided they are suitable for military service."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duty of local board is to accept volunteers first and then select additional individuals as necessary to fill the local quota; volunteers must meet suitability/medical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical examination, induction, training, and service liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected individuals will be examined by a local medical examiner and, if accepted, "will be inducted into the service. The men drafted will receive initially twelve months of training. They will be liable for service anywhere in the Western Hemisphere, in United States possessions outside the hemisphere and in the Philippine islands."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes expected conditions in service: led, clothed, fed, armed and adequately trained; medical examiners determine fitness; induction follows acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay and initial terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure raises regular army pay for privates from $21 to $30 a month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of explanatory text on conditions for draftees; tied to the initial twelve months of training and induction terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employers' and agencies' obligations to facilitate registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The President's proclamation "urges all employers and government agencies of all kinds—Federal, State and local—to give those under their charge sufficient time off in which to fulfill the obligation of registration."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call for full cooperation of employers and agencies to ensure effective and complete registration; local election officials and patriotic citizens also urged to offer services as registration board members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government powers over industry and penalties for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The law provides that the Government may take over and operate, with payment of compensation, the factory of any manufacturer who rejects Government orders; such a manufacturer would face possible maximum penalties of five years' imprisonment and $10,000 fine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as part of the Act's provisions to keep armament production abreast of need; indicates strong governmental authority to enforce production priorities during mobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations subject to change; dependency scrutiny in emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations will be subject to change at any time; although married men living with their wives could expect exemption in the first draft (presumed to have dependents), "If war or some other emergency demanded a large number of men in quick order, the dependency status of married men undoubtedly would be subject to close scrutiny."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial procedures may be liberal regarding dependents, but rules can be tightened depending on needs; local boards may investigate claims of dependency (e.g., divorced men paying alimony or supporting children).
